fullPassage:
[1번] People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.

[2번] In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.

[3번] In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.

[4번] Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.

[5번] Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."

[6번] The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.

[7번] Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

[8번] Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.

③ shifts — 'This melting raises sea levels and ③ shifts the planet's mass(질량을 이동시킨다)'는 raises와 병렬된 단수 동사, 적절해요.

det.tip: 주어의 핵심은 The melting(단수). of polar ice에 낚이지 말 것 → has been

det.korean: identical → individual (깃발은 '각각의' 국가의 상징)

③ same: 국기는 대략 같은 크기와 모양 — 적절
④ distorted: 복잡한 무늬는 뒤틀려 보임 — 적절

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혼자 있음이 창의성을 키우되 협력도 필요하다는 것이 요지
det.analysis:
① 언제나 혼자가 가장 좋다? 본문은 필요할 때만 고독을 찾고 협력도 필요하다고 했으니 지나침 — 오답
② 어릴 때부터 컴퓨터를 배워야 함? 본문에 없음 — 오답
③ 혼자만의 시간은 창의성을 키우지만 협력도 함께 필요함: 본문 전체를 정확히 요약 ←정답
④ 내성적 성격은 고쳐야 할 단점? 본문은 내성적 성격을 창의성의 원천으로 보므로 반대 — 오답
det.tip: 혼자 시간 → 창의성 ↑, 그러나 협력도 필요 (균형)

ch: 창의성을 위해서는 언제나 혼자 있는 것이 가장 좋다.
성공하려면 어릴 때부터 컴퓨터를 배워야 한다.
혼자만의 시간은 창의성을 키우지만 협력도 함께 필요하다.
내성적인 성격은 반드시 고쳐야 할 단점이다.

det.korean: ④ 원문은 마침표 있는 문장을 '덜 진실하게' 느꼈다고 함 → '더 진실하다'는 거짓 → 불일치
det.analysis:
① 마침표 생략이 마침표를 인식하는 방식에 영향을 줌 — 일치
② 친구에게 선생님식으로 말하면 이상하게 들림 — 일치
③ 마침표 사용이 격식 불일치 같은 어색함을 줄 수 있음 — 일치
④ 참가자들은 마침표 있는 문장을 '덜(less)' 진실하게 느꼈어요. '더 진실하다'는 정반대이므로 불일치 ←정답
det.tip: with a period = less sincere(덜 진실). '더 진실하다'는 본문과 반대

ch: 마침표 생략은 우리가 마침표를 인식하는 방식에 영향을 주었다.
친구에게 선생님에게 하듯 말하면 어색하게 들릴 것이다.
문자에 마침표를 쓰면 격식 없는 상황에 격식 있는 말을 쓰는 듯한 어색함을 줄 수 있다.
실험 참가자들은 마침표가 있는 문장을 없는 문장보다 더 진실하다고 느꼈다.

In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, ①<u>causing</u> unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are ②<u>finding</u> nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that ③<u>comes</u> out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were ④<u>bleeding</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: finding → found (many of which are found: 수동태이므로 과거분사)
det.analysis:
① causing: 'causing unique forms of life to develop' 앞 절 전체를 받는 분사구문(능동) — 적절

② finding: 'many of which are ___ nowhere else'에서 동식물은 '발견되는' 대상이에요. be동사(are) 뒤에 수동태를 만들려면 과거분사 found가 와야 해요. finding(능동)은 틀림 ←정답

③ comes: 'a substance that comes out' 선행사 substance가 단수라 관계사절 동사도 -s — 적절

④ bleeding: 'as if the tree were bleeding' 가정법 진행형 — 적절
det.tip: be동사 + 과거분사 = 수동태 → are found (발견되다)

questions.passage: Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ②가 본문(For the first time ever ... subtracting a single second)과 일치
det.analysis:
① 불일치 — 'For the first time ever(사상 처음으로)'라고 했으니 과거에 여러 차례 시행된 적이 없어요.

② 일치 — 지구가 빨라져 '사상 처음으로' 1초를 빼는 것을 고려한다는 본문 내용 그대로예요 ←정답

③ 불일치 — 핵의 활동은 '약 50년 동안(approximately 50 years)' 영향을 주었어요. 5년이 아니에요.

④ 불일치 — 온난화로 얼음이 녹는 것은 자전을 '상쇄·감속'시켜요. 자전을 빠르게 하는 주된 원인은 핵의 활동이에요.
det.tip: 사상 처음으로 1초를 빼는 방안 논의 → ② 일치

ch: 마이너스 윤초는 과거에도 여러 차례 시행되어 온 익숙한 조정이다.
지구의 자전이 빨라지면서 사상 처음으로 시간에서 1초를 빼는 방안이 논의되고 있다.
핵의 불규칙한 활동은 지난 5년 동안만 지구 자전에 영향을 주었다.
지구온난화는 지구의 자전을 더 빠르게 만드는 주된 원인이다.

questions.passage: The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핵심: 깃발이 군대 구별에서 국가 상징으로 발전한 역사 + 국기가 단순한 색·무늬를 쓰는 이유
det.analysis:
① 국기의 역사적 기원과 단순한 디자인의 이유: 글 전체(기원→현대 국가 상징→단순한 무늬를 쓰는 이유)를 포괄 ←정답
② 전쟁 전술: 도입 예시일 뿐 주제 아님
③ 색이 다른 문화적 배경: 본문에 없는 내용
④ 국기 관리 방법: 글의 소재가 아님
det.tip: 기원 + 발전 + 단순 디자인의 이유 = 글 전체

ch: 국기의 역사적 기원과 단순한 디자인의 이유
나라마다 국기 색이 다른 문화적 배경

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문 S3+S5 'took in water to obtain hydrogen', 'released oxygen as waste'를 바꿔 말함 → 일치
det.analysis:
① 산소가 풍부한 대기에서 진화? 당시 대기는 '무산소(oxygen-free)' 상태였음 — 불일치
② 몇 년 만에 급격히? 본문은 '수억 년에 걸쳐 서서히(slowly ... over hundreds of millions of years)' — 불일치
③ 물을 흡수해 수소를 얻고 부산물로 산소를 내보냄 = 'took in water to obtain hydrogen' + 'released oxygen as waste'를 바꿔 말함 ←정답(일치)
④ 메탄의 양을 늘림? 산소는 메탄을 '대체(displacing)'하며 줄였음 — 불일치
det.tip: 물 흡수→수소 획득→산소를 노폐물로 방출 = 본문 핵심 흐름(일치)

ch: 남세균은 산소가 풍부한 대기에서 처음 진화하였다.
지구 대기의 산소량 증가는 단 몇 년 만에 급격히 일어났다.
남세균은 물을 흡수해 수소를 얻고 그 부산물로 산소를 내보냈다.
대기로 올라온 산소는 메탄과 반응하여 메탄의 양을 늘렸다.

questions.passage: Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 역사 속 위대한 예술가와 사상가들이 어떻게 살았는지를 나타낸 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: by themselves = 그들 스스로(혼자서)
det.analysis: 본문 'Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves'에서 위대한 예술가와 사상가들은 '스스로(혼자서)' 살았다고 했어요. 그 표현은 by(전치사) + themselves(재귀대명사) = by themselves(2단어)예요.
det.tip: have lived by themselves = 그들 스스로(혼자서) 살았다

questions.passage: People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods.  In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one.  This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 'something' 뒤에 이어져 '~라고 불리는'이라는 의미를 만드는 과거분사 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: called = ~라고 불리는 (명사 뒤에서 명사를 꾸미는 과거분사)
det.analysis: 본문 'something called "situational code-switching"'에서 called는 '~라고 불리는'이라는 뜻으로 앞의 something을 꾸며요. 명사 뒤에서 '~되는/~된'이라는 뜻으로 꾸밀 때 쓰는 과거분사예요. call(부르다) → called(불리는).
det.tip: something __________ "..." = something이 '~라고 불리는' → 과거분사 called

questions.passage: In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.
questions.stem: 1800년대 아일랜드 사람들이 감자를 무엇으로 사용했는지 본문에서 찾아 3단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: basic food source = 기본 식량(원천)
det.analysis: 본문 'the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source.' — 감자를 사용한 용도 = basic food source(기본 식량)
det.tip: used potatoes as their _____ → basic food source(기본 식량)

questions.passage: We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have __________ (turn) one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: turn(바꾸다) → turned (have + 과거분사: 현재완료)
det.analysis: 동사 turn을 과거분사 turned로 바꿔요. 'We have turned ~ into ~'는 '우리는 ~을 …으로 바꿔 왔다'라는 현재완료예요. have 뒤에는 과거분사가 오므로 turn을 turned로 바꿔야 해요. 'turn A into B'는 'A를 B로 바꾸다'라는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: have + 과거분사 = 현재완료. turn A into B(A를 B로 바꾸다) → have turned

questions.passage: Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 이 섬이 겪는 두 가지 혹독한 기후 조건을 나타내는 부분을, 본문에서 찾아 5단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: extreme heat and frequent droughts = 극심한 더위와 잦은 가뭄
det.analysis: 본문 'Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts'에서 섬이 겪는 두 가지 혹독한 기후 조건 = extreme heat(극심한 더위) and frequent droughts(잦은 가뭄). 형용사+명사 두 쌍을 and로 연결. = 5단어.
det.tip: experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts → 두 기후 조건
